moments.title: Oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz have sharply rebounded: Persian Gulf crude oil exports surpassed 14 million barrels per day last week for the first time since the Iran War began on February 28th. This marks an over +21
moments.selftext: Oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz have sharply rebounded: Persian Gulf crude oil exports surpassed 14 million barrels per day last week for the first time since the Iran War began on February 28th. This marks an over +210% increase from the ~4.5 million barrels per day low seen in March. As a result, the 4-week average is up to 14 million barrels per day, the highest level in 6 months. Persian Gulf crude oil exports have now recovered to ~80% of their pre-war levels. This comes as the US military has increasingly secured the Strait of Hormuz and established a two-way shipping corridor along the coast of Oman, allowing oil convoys to resume through the waterway. Meanwhile, refined fuel shipments, including gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, remain at only around 50% of pre-war levels, as these products are more expensive to transport than crude oil and some refineries in the Persian Gulf that were damaged during the early stages of the war have also yet to fully resume operations. Oil flows are coming back, but the fuel market is still under intense pressure.

moments.title: AI-related employment is surging: AI-linked roles have accounted for more than +750,000 new jobs created in the US since 2023, according to LinkedIn estimates. This surge has been led by data annotators, with +282,000 ne
moments.selftext: AI-related employment is surging: AI-linked roles have accounted for more than +750,000 new jobs created in the US since 2023, according to LinkedIn estimates. This surge has been led by data annotators, with +282,000 new positions created, followed by data center jobs at +117,000, and AI engineers at +105,000. As a result, these 3 categories have accounted for +504,000 new jobs. AI-related positions also offer significantly higher pay, with a median salary of ~$180,000 on LinkedIn, compared to $80,000 across all jobs. This comes as the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, particularly the buildout of data centers, is driving stronger demand for labor. The AI boom is reshaping the US job market.

moments.title: 2027 will shock us all, even the biggest optimists. The ramp up in humanoid robot production will still be relatively slow. By that, I mean only a fraction of people will actually be able to buy one next year. So what I
moments.selftext: 2027 will shock us all, even the biggest optimists. The ramp up in humanoid robot production will still be relatively slow. By that, I mean only a fraction of people will actually be able to buy one next year. So what I mean is, of course AI and its consequences. There will be many insane moments when capabilities suddenly jump, entire categories of work get disrupted almost overnight, and things that looked years or decades away become normal within weeks. 2027 could be the first year when the productive work done by AI agents exceeds the work done by roughly 4-5 billion people (essentially the entire global workforce), with all of that happening in knowledge work rather than physical labor. Agents/AGIs/ASIs will operate at beyond top human expert levels. The amount of useful intellectual work being produced could become almost impossible to comprehend. 2027 could feel like 100 years worth of progress compressed into a single year. It will be an utterly insane year.
